name: Prospectus Content and Disclosure Requirements
description: UK Prospectus Regulation (retained EU 2017/1129) requires the prospectus to contain all information necessary for investors to make an informed assessment of the issuer, the securities, and the rights attached to them. Key mandatory disclosure items include a summary, risk factors, issuer description, financial statements, use of proceeds, and operational and financial review.

name: FCA Prospectus Approval and Review Procedure
description: A prospectus must be approved by the FCA as competent authority before publication. The FCA has a 10 working day review period (20 working days for first-time issuers). A Supplementary Prospectus must be filed within 2 working days of any new material information arising before the Issue Date. Investors have a 2 working day right of withdrawal after a Supplement is published.

name: Market Abuse Regulation — Inside Information and Disclosure
description: UK MAR Article 17 requires prompt public disclosure of inside information and Article 18 requires maintenance of an insider list. Provisions must address management of inside information, notification of listed persons, and delay justification procedures. Violations constitute criminal offences under FSMA 2000.

name: MiFIR Transaction Reporting
description: MiFIR Article 26 requires investment firms to report transactions in financial instruments to their competent authority by T+1 through an Approved Reporting Mechanism. Firms must also report reference data to FIRDS (ESMA) and UK FIRDS (FCA) for newly issued instruments. Product governance under MiFID II requires target market assessment before distribution.

name: Securities Identification and ISIN Assignment
description: All new securities issuances require ISIN assignment under ISO 6166, Common Code (for Euroclear/Clearstream), CUSIP (for DTCC/US clearing), CFI code (ISO 10962), and FISN (ISO 18774). Identifiers must be confirmed by the registrar and reported to relevant clearing systems before closing.

name: Indenture Covenants and Compliance Obligations
description: New issuance documentation must include clearly defined covenants, including limitation on indebtedness, limitation on restricted payments, limitation on liens, limitation on asset sales, change of control provisions, and reporting covenants. Compliance certificates must be delivered periodically to the trustee.

name: Events of Default — Notification and Cure
description: Issuers must notify the Trustee within a specified period (typically 2 Business Days) of knowledge of any Event of Default. Events of Default include payment failures, material covenant breaches, cross-default provisions, bankruptcy, and invalidity of security. Cure periods must be clearly specified.

name: Legal Readiness and Closing Conditions
description: Issuance closing conditions require board resolutions, guarantor authorisations, legal opinions confirming enforceability, no-litigation certificates, and bring-down representation certificates. Each must be filed with the Trustee before the Issue Date.

name: Periodic Reporting Obligations to Trustee and Noteholders
description: Issuers must deliver annual accounts (within 120 days of fiscal year end), quarterly compliance certificates (within 45 days of quarter end), and prompt notice of events of default and material changes. Financial statements must be IFRS-compliant and audited annually.

name: Sanctions and AML Screening for New Issuances
description: All underwriters and bookrunners must complete OFAC and HMT/OFSI sanctions screening of all transaction parties before closing. KYC/AML verification must be completed for each investor. Results must be documented and no-sanctions certificates must be delivered. Obligations arise under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002, Terrorism Act 2000, and applicable OFAC regulations.

name: Stabilisation — Rules and Disclosure
description: Stabilisation activities permitted under Article 5 of UK MAR may be conducted for up to 30 days after the Issue Date by the designated Stabilising Manager. The fact of possible stabilisation must be disclosed in the Prospectus. All stabilisation must be reported to the FCA in accordance with Technical Standards.

name: Consent Solicitation and Indenture Amendments
description: Amendments to the Indenture require the consent of the Required Holders (majority of outstanding principal). Certain fundamental amendments require unanimous consent. Consent solicitations must be disclosed to all Noteholders at least 20 days before the deadline and must fully disclose the purpose and effect of the proposed amendment.

name: ESG and Sustainability Disclosures
description: Issuers listed on UK regulated markets must comply with TCFD-aligned disclosures in annual reports per FCA Listing Rules. Modern Slavery Act statements must be published annually for UK entities with turnover over GBP 36 million. Green Bond or Sustainability Bond designation requires adherence to ICMA principles.
